issues.description: Visibility mismatch for Animal class members: the problem statement (UML and explicit instruction) requires the Animal constructor and the name getter/setter to use protected visibility, but the solution implementation declares them as public. Specifically, problem_statement.md (UML: lines 26-31) indicates a protected constructor and protected getName()/setName(), and the textual instruction (lines 86-89) explicitly asks for protected getter and setter. In the solution file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java the constructor (line 6) and the methods getName() (line 10) and setName(...) (line 14) are declared public. This inconsistency can confuse students about the intended access level and may cause grading scripts or tests that expect protected visibility to fail or grade incorrectly.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the problem specification: change the Animal constructor and the name getter and setter to protected visibility. Concretely, update src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java to use 'protected Animal(String name) { ... }', 'protected String getName() { ... }', and 'protected void setName(String newName) { ... }'. If the solution intentionally exposes them as public, update the problem statement to reflect that public visibility is acceptable and remove the explicit protected requirement to avoid confusion.
